title: Ansel and the Choir
premise: Ivo Quintana, a scribe indentured to the temple of Saint Vellum, has spent her life copying prayers that no god answers — until the old gods of Thornfell wake and begin replying, violently. When the temple's choirboy Ansel is revealed to be the vessel of a soul sold decades ago to the court beneath the mountain, Ivo is blackmailed into guiding a ragged party of priests, smugglers, and one very old god's avatar through the smugglers' roads to steal that soul back. But the debt was signed by Ivo's own grandmother, and the court beneath the mountain holds a claim on Ivo too: the soul they want back is partly hers. In the end Ivo must decide whether to surrender her own half-soul to save Ansel — or break the contract by giving the old gods the one thing they truly hunger for: a mortal who chooses them freely, restoring the choir of voices beneath the mountain and freeing both Ansel and herself.
about_author: Ulyana Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes in the Carpathians before turning to fiction. Her debut novel was shortlisted for the Silverbough Prize, and she writes at the edge of maps, where the roads stop being sure of themselves.

chapters.title: Ink That Answers Back
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Copying prayers in the temple scriptorium, Ivo notices one petition has been answered in handwriting not her own. The temple hides it; she keeps the page. Emotional beat: the thrill and dread of a world that suddenly works differently than she was taught.

chapters.title: The Choirboy Who Hums in His Sleep
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ansel, the temple's foundling choirboy, begins singing harmonies no one taught him — and the candles gutter in time. Ivo realizes the answered prayer was his. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; Ivo, friendless by design, starts to care.

chapters.title: The Abbot's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Abbot catches her with the page and reveals Ansel's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain — and the debt-holder's name is Quintana. He orders her to guide a retrieval party or lose her freedom. Emotional beat: betrayal; charity was a cage all along.

chapters.title: A Party of Inconvenient Saints
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She meets her companions: a defrocked priest, a deaf cartographer, a mercenary who prays to the wrong god, and the Abbot's cold-eyed enforcer, Serel. Emotional beat: wary comedy; a found-family assembling under duress.

chapters.title: The First Road Under Thornfell
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She leads them through smugglers' tunnels she knows by heartbeat, but the mountain has changed — old shrines glow, and something below is counting footsteps. Emotional beat: competence and unease; home terrain turned strange.

chapters.title: What the Mercenary Prays To
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The mercenary confesses his god was eaten by the court beneath the mountain, and he felt it happen. He joins Ivo's secret plan to keep Ansel from being used as bait. Emotional beat: grief disguised as gruffness.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A mountain village has traded its collective memory to the court for a good harvest; the residents smile at strangers they can't recognize. Serel wants to press on; Ivo stays to help. Emotional beat: the true cost of debts, made visible.

chapters.title: Ansel, Dreaming Downward
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Asleep, Ansel walks the court beneath the mountain and meets the Choir — souls woven into a single singing thing. One voice, his grandmother's, tells him to run. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror; he is wanted, and that is not comfort.

chapters.title: The Avatar at the Shrine of Nine Bells
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The party meets the avatar of the old god Vesh — a woman made of bell-sound and borrowed faces — who claims the waking gods need Ansel as their door back into the world. Emotional beat: the rescuers realize they may be thieves working for another thief.

chapters.title: Serel's Report
chapters.summary: Serel's POV. The enforcer secretly reports the party's route to the Abbot, who intends to hand Ansel to Vesh in exchange for the temple's own ancient debt being forgiven. Emotional beat: cold ambition; Serel believes sacrifice is simply arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Signed Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. To cross into the deep roads, each traveler must sign away a memory to a tollkeeper ghost. Ivo signs and loses her memory of her grandmother's face — and finds the debt-contract's seal burned into what remains. Emotional beat: the past is literally the toll.

chapters.title: Half a Soul
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, fractured. The toll unmoors her; she relives her grandmother selling something at the mountain's mouth years ago. The party realizes the court's claim on Ansel is entangled with a claim on Ivo herself. Emotional beat: identity shaken; inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map of the Underside
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The deaf cartographer has been mapping the court by vibration all along; her charts reveal the Choir's heart and a way in that even the gods have forgotten. Emotional beat: quiet heroism; the overlooked one holds the true map.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Serel seizes Ansel and delivers him to Vesh's servants at the boundary of the court, trading him for the temple's absolution. Brannoc is gravely wounded covering the escape. Emotional beat: fury and despair; the party shattered.

chapters.title: Negotiating With a Hungry God
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confronts Vesh's avatar alone and learns the truth: the old gods don't want Ansel — they want a free mortal voice to rejoin their Choir, and the Abbot's plan would give them a slave instead, corrupting the gods themselves. Emotional beat: the enemy's logic, understood too well.

chapters.title: Descent Into the Court
chapters.summary: Ivo, Brannoc, and Odile's POV, braided. Using Odile's vibration-map, the three infiltrate the court beneath the mountain, past galleries of traded memories and corridors that sing back your own voice. Emotional beat: dread and resolve; the deepest dark is made of bargains.

chapters.title: The Choir Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel, caged in the Choir, has begun to dissolve into harmony — losing his name, his fear, himself. He hears Ivo coming and must choose whether to call for help or spare her the price. Emotional beat: the horror of belonging without self.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Contract
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the court's archive, Ivo finds her grandmother's contract: she sold half her own soul to buy the village's memory back, and that half passed to Ivo — which is why Ansel's soul, woven from the same rite, is bound to her. Emotional beat: inheritance reunderstood as love, mispriced.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The court's Regent offers the trade: Ansel's soul for Ivo's half. Ivo almost signs — then realizes any signature feeds the court forever. She tears the contract and offers Vesh instead a freely given voice, sung, not sold. Emotional beat: the climax of choice over transaction.

chapters.title: The Unbought Song
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. Ivo sings her half-soul back into the Choir freely; the court's economy of stolen voices breaks, the Regent unravels, and Ansel is released whole while the old gods, fed by a gift instead of a theft, wake gentler. Emotional beat: catharsis; power uncorrupted at last.

chapters.title: Ledgers Burned
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They surface to find the Abbot exposed, Serel vanished with his records, and the temple's debts void — the old gods now answer only uncoerced prayers. Brannoc and Odile choose to stay in Thornfell; Ivo's indenture is ash. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom; some companions are for a road, not a home.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Choir
chapters.summary: Ansel's and Ivo's POVs, alternating. Ansel, whole, sings in the temple choir — but the old gods listen from the mountain and he sings for both audiences now. Ivo, free and half-her-own-ghost, takes work as a guide for pilgrims walking willingly. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not owed; the road home.
